company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even without an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, implying organic EPS of roughly 42 cents. Sales disappointed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the consensus $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS range of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman remaining through the transition date. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The appointment signals leadership stability as the company works through its interim period.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against an expected 13.85%, as management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing household budgets. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4% but slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate. Some bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% surge in the North American towable RV order backlog year-over-year, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The data reinforces the drug's competitive positioning in the increasingly crowded obesity and metabolic disease space. The pre-market spike reflects strong investor enthusiasm for the clinical readout.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd, covering six names reporting before the open. No broad macro or Fed commentary in today's note — let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share, coming in at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03. But this is a low-quality beat — the upside was driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed significantly, coming in at plus 1.6% versus the expected plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and sounded constructive on fiscal 2027, but the core print is hard to get excited about.

Next, Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a clear strategic bet on robotics and Physical AI — bullish for Cognex's long-term positioning.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid fiscal first quarter beat — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and importantly, they would have beaten even stripping out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, putting organic EPS at roughly 42 cents. Sales missed at $923 million versus the expected $943 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed modestly, but EPS guidance was left unchanged. A mixed print overall, but the quality of the earnings beat is better than it looks on the surface.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st. Hau has prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. Transition news — not a major catalyst either way.

THOR Industries missed fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share at 78 cents versus the expected 87 cents. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management's tone was cautious, citing stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets through the key selling season. The company isn't providing formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall, which limits near-term visibility. The North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year, which is a genuine bright spot, but the headline print and qualitative commentary lean bearish.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is spiking in pre-market after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, with participants showing 22% weight loss. That is a strong data readout and the pre-market reaction reflects it. Watch this one closely at the open — obesity drug data prints tend to move fast and violently in both directions.

Bottom line for the session: Viking is the high-momentum name to watch. AutoZone and THOR are both prints where the details are worse than the headlines suggest. Cognex's RealSense acquisition is a long-term positive. Stay nimble.
